mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between UNRATE < 5% for two months and S&P 500 60-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its previous 12-month average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between INDPRO contraction and S&P 500 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in UNRATE and a fall of at least 0.5% in PAYEMS within the same month indicates a significant deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during months meeting the joint UNRATE and PAYEMS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a monthly decline of more than 0.2% in real personal consumption expenditures (implied from GDPC1 growth and RSAFS dynamics) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces demand and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between the RSAFS/GDPC1 trigger and S&P 500 60-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate that is below the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) for four consecutive months signals a negative real interest rate environment, which incentivizes borrowing and capital expenditure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained negative real rates.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 2% in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) signals a robust recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related industries and overall economic activity, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in months with HOUST > +2.0%.
